# Pidgeon

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolmaster at Brierley school  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Teddy Pidgeon  <sub>[v1 c18 P6](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0006)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Pidgeon twirls his mustache while in the classroom.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011)_

## Personality

He uses sarcasm and a mocking tone with his students when disciplining them, which makes him disliked by pupils like Nell. He is easily distracted from his teaching duties by romantic pursuits or personal poetry writing. He is also willing to admit when he provokes a student, but can be rigid in enforcing punishments.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P42](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0042), [v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044), [v1 c15 P61](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0061), [v1 c15 P65](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0065), [v1 c15 P68](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0068)_

## Traits

- Sarcastic and mocking toward students  <sub>[v1 c15 P61](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0061), [v1 c15 P65](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0065)</sub>
- Easily distracted by romantic interests  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c15 P25](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0025), [v1 c15 P68](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0068)</sub>

## Abilities

- Teaching subjects such as reading, geography, history, dictation, and algebra  <sub>[v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c15 P31](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0031)</sub>
- Writing poetry and delivering dramatic recitations  <sub>[v1 c15 P68](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0068), [v1 c19 P40](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0040)</sub>

## Goals

- Courting Sukey Pullen and helping her prepare for the Regent's Academy entrance exam  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c18 P10](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0010)</sub>

## History

Mr. Pidgeon serves as the schoolmaster at the Brierley school, where he spends much of his time assisting the sixteen-year-old Sukey Pullen with her studies and attempting to court her. During lessons, he frequently ignores the younger children or writes romantic notes and poetry. On one occasion, after Hugh Carrow teases Nell Harcourt about her red hair, causing her to smash her slate over Hugh's head, Mr. Pidgeon disciplines Nell by forcing her to stand at the blackboard and writing a derogatory note about her temper above her head. Later, when a group of students arrives late after picking spruce gum, he singles out Nell as a victim and forces her to sit next to Hugh Carrow. Deeply insulted by his treatment, Nell refuses to return to school for the remainder of the term. At the Debating Club concert in Mr. Gorham Pullen's field, Mr. Pidgeon delivers a moving recitation of Mark Antony's address above the body of Caesar, directing his emotional delivery toward Sukey Pullen.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c15 P31](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0031), [v1 c15 P40](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0040), [v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044), [v1 c15 P46](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0046), [v1 c15 P60](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0060), [v1 c15 P61](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0061), [v1 c15 P68](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0068), [v1 c15 P77](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0077), [v1 c15 P81](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0081), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091), [v1 c19 P40](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0040)_

## Background by volume

- Landed his teaching position at Brierley school because his uncle is a school trustee  <sub>[v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091)</sub>
- Is considered a fine student by some, though criticized by local homemakers for poor discipline and ignoring younger pupils to focus on older ones  <sub>[v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091), [v1 c18 P6](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0006)</sub>
